speaker: Doctor
text: I see the newborn presenting with respiratory distress; have you noticed any cyanosis or grunting respirations since birth? Did the mother have any infections like CMV or Toxoplasmosis during pregnancy? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Blood_Culture, Chest_XRay.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of grunting, retractions, and peripheral cyanosis in a newborn is highly suggestive of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) or Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN). REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas, Blood_Glucose. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay results?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the arterial blood gas and glucose results are normal, are there any signs of pulmonary edema, and was there a history of maternal diabetes or prolonged labor? REQUEST TEST: Maternal_History_Review.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN)
